observations: A large rounded head shape fills most of the canvas, outlined in thick black lines against a flat grey background, with a broad yellow band sweeping across the upper third.
Two eye zones are built from overlapping looping circles in purple, blue, and red; the left reads as a tight spiral, the right as a rectangular recess with smaller scribbled marks inside.

A mouth near the lower centre shows white rectangular tooth shapes framed in red and black hatching, with a dark gap visible between the rows; loose lines in pink, teal, and green scatter across the face and spill beyond the head outline.
reading: The head pushes close to the frame, leaving little open space around it. Layered loops mark the eyes with a wound-up, restless quality, while the exposed tooth rows and dark gap between them sit somewhere between a shout and a grimace. The grey ground keeps the yellow band and scattered colour lines from merging into noise, giving each hue a moment before the next crowds in.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnxyz-other subset, nnxyz #3 sits between title neighbours nnxyz #2 and nnxyz #4. Where nnxyz #2 packs multiple head forms into a near-black field, this work isolates one head on grey, making the yellow sweep and looping eye marks the dominant structural moves.

nnxyz nnotb #178 centres a single rounded head with asymmetric eye treatments—one concentric spiral, one smaller enclosed symbol—offering a direct parallel to the eye-zone construction here, though set on an olive ground.

lookingQuestion: How does the grey ground change the way the yellow band and the looping eye marks compete for your attention compared to the darker grounds in the comparison works?
ambiguities: The rectangular form at the upper left edge of the head is ambiguous—it reads as either an ear or an attached object, and the image does not resolve this clearly.
